newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli provident funds post inflow in December.
newsitem.headline: Israeli provident funds post inflow in December.

text.p: Israeli provident funds registered net accruals of 397.4 million shekels in December, marking the first time in 1996 they enjoyed a net inflow of money, the Finance Ministry said on Tuesday.

For all of 1996, the funds had net withdrawals of 11.9 billion shekels, compared with 5.77 billion in 1995. The funds, which have seen a steady outflow of money since 1994, suffered a big wave of withdrawals in July and August, prompting a collapse of bond prices.
Since then, the level of redemptions has steadily fallen, to 1.1 billion shekels in October and 382 million in November.

The funds usually enjoy a net inflow in December, as investors take advantage towards year-end of tax benefits offered by the funds. In December 1995, however, the funds suffered net redemptions of 495,000 shekels.

The Treasury said savings schemes had a net inflow of 161.2 million shekels, as savers deposited 294.1 million shekels in inflation-index programmes and withdrew a net 133 million from foreign currency-linked programmes.
The inflow marked a turnaround from November, when savings schemes suffered a net outflow of 201.3 million shekels.
For all of 1996, savings programmes had a net influx of money totaling 5.36 billion shekels.
